newsitem.title: USA: Suspects held in Los Angeles freeway attacks.
newsitem.headline: Suspects held in Los Angeles freeway attacks.

text.p: At least two men were in custody on Thursday as possible suspects in a rash of freeway vandalism that has shattered the windows of more than 200 cars and trucks on Los Angeles area freeways in a month.

The men were among three arrested in Los Angeles by the California Highway Patrol (CHP) on Wednesday night when officers stopped their car and found "paraphernalia of the kind that could clearly have been used in these suspected slingshot window breakings," California Gov. Pete Wilson told reporters in Sacramento on Wednesday.
Reports on local television that one of the suspects was released on Thursday morning could not immediately be confirmed. The CHP planned a news conference later in the day.

Officers also found a sawed-off shotgun and a 9mm handgun in the suspects' car but police said they were unlikely to be the weapons used in the attacks. They suspect the 240 rear windows broken since the attacks started on Sept. 11 were shattered by pellet guns or pellets propelled by slingshots as they are capable of shattering tempered glass but not of penetrating it. None of the projectiles has been found.

Wilson, stressing authorities did not believe the suspects acted alone in the window-smashing spree, told reporters: "We are very pleased because it would seem we have information that will lead to the arrest of at least some of those who have been involved in this very, very dangerous and foolish business of sniping the rear windows of moving vehicles."

The governor said authorities would seek severe punishment for anyone charged in the attacks. "This is a very serious business. It is not a prank. We will not treat it as a prank. It is assault with a deadly weapon."
